title: Reduce syscall overhead in observability hotpath and upgrade OpenTelemetry gracefully
creator: Anika Rao
description: This ticket consolidates several small-but-costly observability tech-debt items: upgrade the OpenTelemetry SDK/collector pipeline to the latest compatible release, reduce per-request syscall overhead caused by synchronous span/log flushes, and introduce a graceful shutdown/flush path to avoid data loss during deployments. The goal is to lower CPU and syscall count on the inference hotpath and stabilize tail latency during high QPS bursts.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK and collector components to the chosen target version with verified compatibility tests
Reduce syscall count from the runtime hotpath by at least 35% in the 99th-percentile benchmark compared to current baseline
No increase in end-to-end request p99 latency beyond 5% under our synthetic multi-tenant load
Graceful shutdown flush completes within configured window (default 5s) with zero span loss in CI smoke tests
Relevant dashboards (cpu, p95/p99 latency, telemetry-drop-rate) added/updated and baseline documented
tasks: Audit current OTEL SDK + collector deps across services and list compat blockers
Introduce an async span/log writer backed by a fixed-size ring buffer to avoid per-request file/socket syscalls
Add an adaptive backpressure policy: when ring buffer is >85% full, drop debug-level spans and increment telemetry counter
Implement graceful shutdown hook that flushes ring buffer and waits up to shutdown.timeout seconds
Run benchmark harness (locust+service-proxy) and collect syscall traces via perf and eBPF for before/after
Open PR(s) and request cross-team review (runtime/instrumentation/platform)
Update Console dashboards and add alerting for dropped-spans-rate > 0.1% and flush-failures
risks: OTEL upgrade may change span/attribute serialization leading to increased payload size — confirm with smoke tests
Ring buffer holds more memory per-process; need to validate under low-memory environments
Aggressive drop policy could hide real customer errors if misconfigured
Graceful shutdown timeout may delay pod termination on some infra; coordinate with infra/eks team
notes: Design decision: prefer a single lightweight in-process async writer over introducing an external sidecar to keep network hops minimal
We will keep the existing sync path behind a feature flag for 2 releases to allow rollback
Benchmarks should run against runtime-1.21 image to ensure kernel and allocator parity
Plan to run canary on 'dedicated-runtime' tier before platform-wide rollout
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed — confirmed two major syscall hotspots: synchronous file/socket write per span and a mutex contention in span-aggregator
2026-02-20: Prototype async writer implemented; local benchmarks show 28% drop in syscalls and 18% lower p95 latency for small payload traces
2026-03-02: OTEL SDK upgrade path evaluated; identified a breaking change in attribute semconv versioning. Added compatibility shim to migration branch
2026-03-08: Infra suggested default shutdown.timeout=5s to balance flush and pod drain time — integrated into PR
2026-03-14: Load test (50k reqs/s synthetic) shows ring buffer prevents syscall amplification; observing rare drop events at sustained burst > 120% capacity — added adaptive drop threshold task
